title: Clear shifts removes only the old lead's whole-work-order shifts
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · Schedule access · about 30 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Three eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Esther Howard", [Tech-B] "Ralph Edwards", [Tech-C] "Dana Ortiz". A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope" (used by this case only) with three Approved work orders led by [Tech-A]: [WO-1] and [WO-2], each with a line "Line 1", and [WO-3].
  • Shifts on the Schedule: [WO-1] - [Tech-A] tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (entire work order) and 13:00–15:00 (Line 1), [Tech-C] tomorrow 8:00–10:00 (entire work order). [WO-2] - the same two [Tech-A] shifts as [WO-1]. [WO-3] - [Tech-A] the day after tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (entire work order).
  • The technician names and the times are used in the expected results and stay as written; the numbers are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Esther Howard" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] = "Ralph Edwards" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-C] = "Dana Ortiz" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (the expected results call it "S1-702"): Lead Technician = [Tech-A]; with a line "Line 1".
    • [WO-2] (the expected results call it "S1-698"): Lead Technician = [Tech-A]; with a line "Line 1".
    • [WO-3] (the expected results call it "S1-691"): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. Line names in this case (such as "Line 1") are only labels for you: the New Line form's "What Are You Doing?" box only offers ready-made lines (typed text finds no results), so pick any ready-made line for each one (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot") and write down which is which.
  7. On the Schedule, give [Tech-A] a shift on [WO-1] tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-A]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  8. On the Schedule, give [Tech-A] a shift on [WO-1] tomorrow 13:00–15:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-A]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Choose lines and tick Line 1 > set the end time > save.
  9. On the Schedule, give [Tech-C] a shift on [WO-1] tomorrow 8:00–10:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-C]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  10. On the Schedule, give [Tech-A] a shift on [WO-3] the day after tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-A]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  11. Give [WO-2] the same two [Tech-A] shifts as [WO-1] (8:00–12:00 entire work order, 13:00–15:00 Line 1).
  12. Check the setup worked: on the Schedule for tomorrow, [Tech-A]'s row shows 8:00–12:00 and 13:00–15:00 on [WO-1] and on [WO-2], [Tech-C]'s row shows 8:00–10:00 on [WO-1]; the day after tomorrow [Tech-A] has 8:00–12:00 on [WO-3]. If a shift is missing or wrong, add or fix it before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Clear Shifts Scope" in Search.
  3. Drag [WO-1] from [Tech-A]'s column into [Tech-B]'s column.
  4. Read the prompt that opens, then click Clear shifts.
  5. Drag [WO-2] from [Tech-A]'s column into [Tech-B]'s column.
  6. In the prompt click Keep shifts.
  7. Open the Schedule for tomorrow and the day after, and read every shift on [WO-1], [WO-2] and [WO-3].
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Both drags open a prompt asking whether to clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts for the whole work order.
  • After Clear shifts: "S1-702" is led by Ralph Edwards, Esther Howard's 8:00–12:00 whole-work-order shift on it is gone, Dana Ortiz's 8:00–10:00 shift on it is still there, and Esther Howard's shift on "S1-691" is untouched.
  • After Keep shifts: "S1-698" is led by Ralph Edwards and both Esther Howard shifts on it are still there.
  • Esther Howard's 13:00–15:00 Line 1 shifts are still there on both work orders: the prompt never clears line shifts.

What you should see today (build v26.40.8-7a95011, 10/8/2026): changing the lead (by dragging the card or with Reassign lead technician) shows no question about scheduled shifts, even when the outgoing lead has a shift booked for the entire work order. The lead changes at once with the "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") message, and the outgoing lead's shift stays on the Schedule. (1) If you see exactly that, mark the case Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results above say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R11, S4-R22, S4-R23, S4-R24, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions DR-31 (optional whole-work-order shift clearing). Schedule shift picker labels "Entire work order" / "Choose lines" from the Schedule suite. Source-verified 8 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R11: “When changing the lead technician in Board View or Tech View, ask whether to clear the outgoing lead’s work-order-level scheduled shifts.”
  • S4-R22: “If the user chooses to clear shifts, remove only the outgoing lead’s shifts scheduled against that whole work order.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”
  • S4-R24: “Never clear shifts scheduled against individual work order lines through this prompt.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
